title: Joint Illumination Enhancement and Feature Preservation for Object Detection in the Dark
abstract: Detecting objects in underexposed scenarios suffers from low contrast and heavy color distortion. We propose an illumination-aware preprocessing network that restores dynamic range while preserving semantic gradients for downstream detectors. On DarkFace, our method improves mAP by 8.2% for both CNN and Transformer detectors.

sections.Abstract: Detecting objects in underexposed scenarios suffers from low contrast and heavy color distortion. We propose an illumination-aware preprocessing network that restores dynamic range while preserving semantic gradients for downstream detectors. On DarkFace, our method improves mAP by 8.2% for both CNN and Transformer detectors.
sections.Introduction: Low illumination severely affects the discriminative capacity of deep detectors. Standard low-light enhancement algorithms often amplify high-frequency sensor noise. We formulate an end-to-end framework where an illumination curve estimation module directly assists object detection heads.
sections.Methodology: The pipeline applies differentiable curve adjustment parameters conditioned on global image statistics. Feature maps from intermediate enhancement layers are fused with the detector backbone.
sections.Experiments: Evaluated on the DarkFace benchmark using standard detection metrics. We compare detectors with and without our illumination-aware module using YOLO and Swin-Transformer backbones.
sections.Results: The proposed illumination preprocessing method improves mAP@0.5 by 8.2% on the DarkFace dataset (from 42.1% to 50.3% mAP). Both CNN and Vision Transformer architectures exhibit substantial gains in precision when local contrast is restored prior to feature extraction.
sections.Conclusion: Explicit illumination preprocessing provides substantial gains for dark scene understanding when trained end-to-end with detection objectives.
